articleTitle: Outlier Detection Approach in Sensor-to-Microcontroller Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of an outlier detection method based on the Grubbs test, specifically designed for microcontroller applications. The theoretical background for outlier detection is outlined, and experimental validation is conducted using a direct sensor-to-microcontroller interface circuit. Results demonstrate that this approach improves the accuracy of measurement systems affected by Gaussian noise or other normal-distributed external interference signals.

articleTitle: Charging Data Analysis and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: This study develops a classification model for Electric Vehicles (EVs) using data from EV charging stations. Utilizing a dataset of six charging sessions, a deep learning algorithms, Auto-Encoders, was implemented to classify EVs based on charging time, energy consumption, and charging patterns. The model's effectiveness is assessed through accuracy and precision, offering insights into optimizing EV charging infrastructure and services.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency of Vehicle-to-Grid Cycle in Real Application
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology in the power engineering area marks a change towards enhancing grid dynamics and elevating energy storage systems. The article presents an empirical analysis of V2G energy efficiency utilizing a Nissan Leaf as the research vehicle. The selected Nissan Leaf exhibits a State of Health (SoH) at 77.3%, accrued mileage of 111 656 km, and displays an estimated range of 148 km on a full charge. The main point of the article topic is the efficacy of energy transfer in an off-grid scenario between the electric vehicle (EV) and the microgrid. The findings indicate that the V2G energy cycle efficiency stands at 68.43 %. These observations contribute to the foundational research necessary for optimizing micro-grid systems. The experiment is contextualized within Central Europe's environmental and microgrid conditions, providing a specific landscape for assessing V2G system viability. This article is a test case for future potential research.

articleTitle: A DC-DC Converter with Extended Voltage Static Gain, Input/Output Continuous Current and Reduced Switch Voltage Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: In recent decades, DC-DC converters have been important to help the penetration of renewable energy sources into the power grid and for use as independent power sources. These power converters are commonly used in many power conversion appliances and portable electronic devices. However, to regulate and convert a photovoltaic (PV) power source voltage to the required output voltage, it is often necessary to use DC-DC converters to provide a stable and adjustable voltage, a feature that most of these converters do not guarantee. Thus, this paper presents a new single-switch DC-DC converter with Boost characteristics. This converter is characterized by extended static voltage gains and input/output currents. Besides, differently to the standard Boost, the voltage stress of the proposed converter switch is lower than the converter output voltage. The proposed converter operating principle and static gain will be examined through theoretical analysis. Some simulation and experimental tests will evaluate its performance and other particularities of this DC-DC converter.

articleTitle: Active Control for Resonance Mitigation in Electric Drive Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: The use of inverter-based motor controllers that can generate fast voltage level transitions is increasing in the field of electric drive systems because of their ability to achieve higher efficiency. However, the fast voltage transitions, dv/dt's, are prone to generate bearing currents and cause overvoltages that may harm the electric motor. An LC filter applied between the inverter and the motor terminals can reduce the dv/dt's. However, the LC filter will cause overvoltage due to resonance but this can be overcome by introducing an extra pulse at each pulse-width modulation (PWM) transition. The timing of this extra pulse is crucial for suppressing the resonance, but due to nonlinearities in a real system, the time instants may vary over time and are thus in need of control. In this study, an analytical expression for the optimal pulse location and duration is derived and we propose a control algorithm that continuously calculates the optimal pulse switch time instants based on the measured output voltage. The control algorithm can handle sudden system disturbances and a Monte Carlo simulation is performed to evaluate the performance of the algorithm. This hybrid filter successfully reduces dv/dt's at the motor terminals while simultaneously eliminating overvoltages due to the filter resonance.

articleTitle: A Novel Double Coupled Inductor Ultra-High Gain Boost Converter for Low-Power Photo-Voltaic
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: Solar power has been the subject of extensive research recently. The boost converter is the main component of any solar power harvester. Coupled inductors have been utilized to increase and extend the voltage gain of the boost converter. This paper introduces a novel converter with double coupled inductors for low power Photo-Voltaic (PV) applications. The proposed topology improves the operating condition of the power harvesting during strong shading concurrently by improving the efficiency and output voltage. It operates with a higher voltage gains and efficiency concurrently at reduced solar irradiation in Continuous Current Mode (CCM). A prototype was successfully tested and an efficiency of 94 % was retained during an overcast with a single stage converter.

articleTitle: Edge AI Acceleration Using OpenCL Framework on NXP i.MX 8M Nano SoM
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: Edge computing brings computational resources closer to the data source by enhancing processing capabilities and reducing the complexity and latency of data transmission. This approach reduces traffic volume and bandwidth requirements for IoT applications while improving response times for real-time operations. Modern edge computing must balance the need for energy efficiency with the demand for high computational performance, particularly in battery-powered devices. Advances in artificial intelligence have intensified the need for efficient inference on resource-constrained devices. Heterogeneous computing systems, which can offload tasks to optimized hardware components, offer a partial solution, though they add complexity for developers. The OpenCL framework helps mitigate this complexity by providing a standardized way to utilize heterogeneous systems. This paper explores the feasibility of performing AI inference on the NXP i.MX 8M Nano processor using OpenCL, addressing the challenges and potential benefits of deploying machine learning models on small” energy-efficient systems.

articleTitle: Efficiency and Full Speed Range Utilization of IPMSM Drives Based on Optimal Control
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: In this paper, efficiency and full speed range utilization of IPMSM drives based on the maximization of torque producing capability are considered. An enhanced closed-loop strategy for controlling the flux reference command in the deep field-weakening region of IPMSM is derived with the addition of novel PI gain tuning based on the Lagrange multiplier method for stable and high performance transient response of high-speed drives. Simulation tests were carried out to verify the robustness and applicability of the proposed algorithm for low-voltage IPMSM traction drive.

articleTitle: Sliding-Mode Based Control Technique for Triple Active Bridge DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: Due to the capability of interfacing various energy sources, storage units and loads, multiport converters (MPCs) are increasingly being considered in distribution system applications. There exist several topologies of MPC being Triple Active bridge (TAB) one of the most relevant. This paper deals with the design of sliding mode control (SMC) for TAB DC-DC converter has been proposed based on reduced order model. In order to built this model, topology-level power decoupling method has been used and the current transformer dynamics has been ignored. Two sliding-control laws have been proposed to regulate output voltages and to control the power flows between the three ports in order to balance the total power. The proposed controller was tested and validated using Matlab/Simulink. It is shown that the designed controller guarantees an efficient power flow sharing and an accurate reference voltage tracking, and it proves a good robustness when the DC-bus voltage and loads are disturbed. Finally, The performance of the designed SMC is compared with conventional PI control. The comparison shows that TAB DC-DC converter under SMC has better dynamic performance and good robustness against sudden load change.

articleTitle: Analysis and Comparison of PI and Reinforcement Learning Controllers for the Dual Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: Currently, power electronic converters have a wide variety of applications, among these converters is the Dual Active Bridge (DAB) converter. Due to its high efficiency and power density, it is attractive and can be used in electric vehicle chargers. The objective of this paper is to present the reinforcement learning (RL) based Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm as an option to control the DAB converter with SPS modulation, replacing the traditional PI control in voltage mode. System simulations and training of the DDPG algorithm were developed in Matlab/Simulink software. Finally, the results show that the RL control achieves a better performance than the PI control, considering the response time to reach the steady-state and avoiding overshoot at different disturbances occurring in the system.

articleTitle: Pioneering CMOS IC Fabrication in Undergraduate Curriculum Using Open-Source CAD Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: In this paper, we present a fabricated, working ring-oscillator designed in a 180 nm standard CMOS process node and using only free and open-source CAD tools. While this topology is well-known, a common practice in all textbooks, the novelty in our work lays in the fact that the silicon-ready design (GDS files) was achieved within an undergrad course with zero investment in industry standard vendor software licenses. The IC is packaged into a DIL16 housing and here we demonstrate correct operation in a breadboard setting using a standard measurement setup.

articleTitle: Power Quality Enhancement of DSTATCOM Using E2PLL-Based Control Method for Wind Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: DSTATCOM is most commonly used to regulate the voltage generated by the SEIG used in wind turbines. DSTATCOM provides the reactive power required by the SEIG and the load. It uses the DC bus voltage to provide the required reactive power. For effective control, the DC bus voltage must be constant at the desired value and the required reactive power must be correctly determined. This also requires correct estimation of the reference source currents. When the system is loaded with non-linear and unbalanced loads, if the load currents are not well filtered, the active and reactive components of the load currents will be incorrectly estimated. In this paper, an E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> PLL-based control algorithm with superior filtering capability is proposed for the control of SEIG loaded with nonlinear and unbalanced load. The proposed algorithm is tested under nonlinear and unbalanced load conditions. The obtained results clearly prove the effectiveness of the E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> PLL-based control algorithm.

articleTitle: Integrated Tuning of Control Loops for a Shaft-Sensorless PMa-SynRM Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: In this paper the dynamic performance of shaft sensorless drive with PMa-SynRM motor are considered. The whole control structure is carefully analyzed and procedure for integrated tuning of all three control loops in drive, FOC current loop, internal speed observer loop and speed loop is proposed. It is believed that combined tuning approach is the only way to assure stable drive performance, insuring separation of all loop bandwidths but still with wanted dynamic speed and torque response. The experimental results on 1kW PMa-SynRM drive working with and without the shaft-sensor prove the effectiveness of proposed tuning procedure.

Author Keywords: Permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance machine (PMa-SynRM)

articleTitle: State of Charge Estimation of Batteries Using a Neural Network Based on Impedance Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: A comparison of the results of battery state of charge estimation using neural networks with different characteristics applied to the results of battery impedance spectroscopy has been performed. The neural networks differed both in dimensions (number of neurons, number of layers, and number of epochs) and in the training optimization algorithm (Levenberg-Marquardt, Bayesian Regularization, BFGS Quasi-Newton, and Conjugate Gradient).

articleTitle: Numerical Optimisation of Air-cooled Heat Sink Geometry to Improve Temperature Gradient of Power Semiconductor Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: This paper discusses the numerical analysis and optimisation of a conventional air-cooled heat sink having an insignificant geometrical modification to reduce the temperature gradient of power semiconductors installed on the top surface of the heat sink. Using the numerical approach, the influence of the geometry modification on the thermal performance of the heat sink was thoroughly analysed. The geometry modification applied to the heat sink is based on the partial removal of the central fins at the air flow intake in the form of a triangle and the integration of a guide plate to provide a reduction in the temperature difference across the heat sink surface. These modifications do not expand the heat sink footprint or make the manufacturing process complicated. The optimised design exhibited a considerably reduced temperature gradient between the power electronic modules. The temperature difference between power semiconductors operating with a power loss of 100 W per module is reduced from 3.779°C (for the unmodified benchmark model) to 0.0018°C. The study findings contribute to the advancement of thermal solutions in power electronics by presenting a manufacturable, scalable, and efficient heat sink design that addresses the industry demand for sustainable thermal regulation.

articleTitle: ASimulated Logistic Algorithm for Distributed Flexible Assembly Flowshop Scheduling with Post-processing
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: An optimized mathematical model has been developed to streamline gas turbine production by targeting the minimization of the overall completion time, known as makespan. The production process is broken down into a series of stages: jobs are processed across multiple parallel factories, assembled into semi-finished goods with flexibility in their assembly order, and then transformed into final products through various stages of additional processing. To initiate solutions, a three-tier composite heuristic is employed, supplemented by six specialized neighborhood structures devised according to the different stages of the problem. Drawing inspiration from natural population growth mechanisms, we introduce a Simulated Logistic Algorithm (SLA) designed for robust solution enhancement. Comparative experiments on both small and extensive scales demonstrate the SLA's superior performance over established optimization techniques such as Particle Swarm Optimization, Tabu Search, and Genetic Algorithms, especially notable in large-scale applications. Thorough mathematical and statistical evaluations reinforce the efficacy of the SLA and validate the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Automated Control of a Coffee Machine - Learning Instrument
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: This paper introduces a practical tutorial aimed at demonstrating the integration of cyber-physical systems across various hierarchical levels. The project involves the automation of a standard coffee machine, enabling it to autonomously prepare multiple beverage options in response to external commands. The tutorial serves as an educational tool for understanding the application of automation technologies in everyday appliances, providing a hands-on learning experience in control systems and automation processes.

articleTitle: Adaptive Gate Driver Architecture for Optimized Slew Rate Control
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: The evolution of power switching devices has been instrumental in meeting the demands of high-efficiency, high-performance applications across various sectors. Key to this advancement is the ability of these devices to handle rapid switching actions. However, the benefits of fast switching are counterbalanced by the challenges it presents in controlling the slew rate during hard switching events-critical for minimizing electromagnetic interference, reducing switching losses, and extending device life. Conventional gate driving solutions are often inadequate to manage the dynamic requirements of modern power switches, prompting the need for more sophisticated control techniques. This paper introduces a versatile gate driver architecture designed to enhance the control of switching transitions in power devices. The proposed system actively senses and regulates the dV/dt slew rate, adjusting the gate driving current in accordance with predetermined set points. This real-time control enables the fine-tuning of the slew rate, ensuring optimized performance across a multitude of operating conditions. The architecture's adaptability also facilitates its application to a wide range of power switches.

articleTitle: Automating the Handling Process of a Coffee Machine Using a Robotic Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: The study RoboCafe explores the automation of a lever-action coffee-making system using a FANUC robotic manipulator controlled by a PLC complying with ISA-88 standards. The robotic arm, equipped with a specialized gripper, is designed to handle various components of the coffee-making system, including operating a lever-action coffee machine and grinder. A virtual simulation of the system was developed to test and validate the system before physical implementation using virtual commissioning techniques. Strength measurement confirmed the robotic arm's capability to exert the required force for coffee machine operation. Using standard industrial communication such as Modbus TCP, the cooperation between heterogenous controllers can be established in case other communication protocol is not supported.

articleTitle: Hosting Capacities of LV Distribution Network with Dispersed and Concentrated PV systems connection
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: Increased integration of photovoltaic (PV) production creates new challenges and opportunities for the Distribution System Operators (DSO). It is crucial to establish comprehensive standards for the maximum integration of PV systems without disrupting normal operations. This paper explores the hosting capacity of concentrated and dispersed PV systems connected to LV network. The aim is to determine the maximum amount of PV generation for the low-voltage network considering voltage, line loads and transformer thermal constraints. Simulations are performed on a model of real power systems in DigSilent Power Factory software. This paper encompasses a wide range of activities vital for the successful integration of PV systems into low voltage distribution network that has been converted into micro-grid. Goal was to ensure stability, security, and efficiency of the grid while exploring best possible ways of connecting new renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Neutral Voltage Modulation in Cascaded H-Bridge Inverters Under DC-Source Voltage Imbalance Using Modified Level-Shifted PWM
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: The operation of a cascaded H-bridge inverter in unbalanced desource voltage conditions necessitates application of a suitable offset voltage injection to achieve extension of the linear modulation index range for balanced three-phase operation. This can be achieved to a certain extent with the min-max offset voltage injection and to an exceedingly greater degree by the so-called neutral voltage modulation (NVM). However, application of these methods using the phase-shifted (PS) pulse width modulation (PWM) leads to suboptimal results in terms of harmonic distortion of the phase voltages and currents, and equal power dissipation of the unequally charged desources - which is not ideal. This paper suggests an alternative application of these offset injections using the in-phase disposition (IPD) level-shifted (LS) PWM method which has been modified accordingly for application in dc-source imbalance conditions. The obtained results show significant performance improvement in the THD of the phase voltages and currents. At the same time, exceedingly greater balancing potential and control over the power distribution of the dc-sources is achieved.

articleTitle: Modelling of Saturation in a Single Phase Transformer by Using Instantaneous Saturation Curve
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: Accurately modeling the saturation present in transformer iron cores, so that it fully reflects all of the effects saturation has on the current waveforms, presents a challenging task. Over the years, several different approaches for modeling transformer saturation have been developed and used. One of the more complex methods includes computing a so-called instantaneous saturation curve, which describes the instantaneous magnetizing flux value against the value of the magnetizing current. This paper offers an experimental verification of the instantaneous curve method for the case of a single-phase transformer using the Humusoft MF 634 acquisition card. The recorded values of no-load voltage and current are used to obtain instantaneous saturation curve which is used in dynamic simulation model. By comparing the waveforms and harmonic content between simulated and recorded currents in the open-circuit experiment for different values of input voltages, we have shown the applicability of the method and demonstrated that we can realistically model the behavior of the transformer, both in linear and saturated modes.

articleTitle: PV Model Parameter Estimation Based on Hybrid Metaheuristic Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: Estimating PV cell model parameters using actual current-voltage data is crucial in determining the functionality of PV systems. Obtaining PV cell model parameters with the help of metaheuristic algorithms is a feasible solution. In this study, single and double-diode PV cell model parameters are obtained using the Salp swarm algorithm (SSA), arithmetic optimization algorithm (AOA), and hybrid SSA-AOA. Polycrystalline TRP-050B PV module current-voltage data are used to improve the applicability and accuracy of the proposed method. The current-voltage data of the PV module were obtained at 27°C and 200 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> irradiance values. The statistical functions of the sum of squares of errors (SSE) and root mean square of the sum of squares of errors (RMSE) were used to evaluate the functionality of the obtained results. According to the obtained results, the recommended hybrid SSA-AOA is demonstrated to be feasible, robust, and realistic.

articleTitle: Design of Servo Drive System for Automatic Packaging/Wrapping Line
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: The design of packaging and wrapping machines demands a high degree of automation to achieve fast and precise coordination of synchronized and dependent motions. Consequently, specially designed mechanical mechanisms are typically employed. However, these motion solutions have limited flexibility which makes them nonoptimal when motion changes are required. In such scenarios, it is often necessary to either install an entirely new mechanism or replace it with a servo drive, which can provide nonuniform motion. The decision to replace the entire mechanism with a servo drive system is widely and effectively implemented in packaging industry nowadays. In this paper the example of application of Siemens hardware and software tools in designing servo drive system for horizontal packaging and wrapping line is presented. The paper provides a brief overview of servo system design using currently available set of tools, which facilitate initial system demand planning, hardware specification, and final design. The process includes equipment defining, configuring, programming, and testing, through a case study of a packaging/wrapping machine designed for specific types of insulation building materials.

articleTitle: Quasi-Resonant Flyback Converter in 800 V System: Industrialization Aspects and Comparison to Active-Clamped Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: This paper presents implementation and some industrialization aspects of the quasi-resonant flyback (QRF) dc-dc converter with valley switching. The QRF was used as an auxiliary power supply of an 800 V system and was supplied from the variable dc-link. The 57 W mock-up was built and tested. A comprehensive comparison of QRF and ACF (active-clamped flyback) dc-dc converters in this emerging application is provided. The both converters had similar specification, the same maximum switching frequency, majority of used parts, the same secondary sides and respective layout-which made comparisons plausible and unique in the literature. Aspects covered were: efficiency, no-load losses, FFT (fast Fourier transformation), EMI (electro-magnetic interference), supply chain, cooling, price, space, complexity, technical cleanliness, insulation coordination and functional safety. The QRF had higher efficiency than ACF in whole load and input voltage range-which was expected since an ACF has higher losses due to circulation energy. For the same reason, losses at no-load conditions were significantly lower with QRF. A comparison of measured drain-source voltages' FFT showed that the spectral content of QRF is a bit dependent on the input voltage and that amplitude of harmonics is a bit higher at 850 V than at 620 V input voltage. Those findings were different compared to the ones with ACF in sense that the spectral content of ACF was independent on the input voltage. So, it was clear that the QRF, in this application, is superior to ACF in every aspect except for FFT and EMI.

articleTitle: Development and Implementation of Model in MATLAB for Hand Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: This study describes a method for measuring flexion and extension motions in the hand, which is crucial for healing and restoring a complete range of motion following accidents. Precise control is essential because of the human hand's intricate anatomy, which consists of various bones and joints. The method replicates the trajectories of the five fingers, emphasizing their position, speed, acceleration, and torque at four crucial structural points: four fingers that stretch to 90 degrees and then return to 0 degrees, with the thumb creating a 20-degree angle, a crucial initial position for successful recovery. The ability to simulate these trajectories is essential for correctly tracking patients' progress and customizing rehabilitation treatments, both of which improve patient care and rehabilitation outcomes.

articleTitle: Analysis of Short Circuit Currents in Large Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator: Dynamic and Simplified Models
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: The paper proposes dynamic and simplified models for calculating three-phase short circuit currents of large permanent magnet generator directly connected to the grid. These models are derived by modifying the dynamic model of permanent magnet synchronous motor to account for direct grid connection and generator loading prior to fault. The applicability of the analyzed models is demonstrated through a series of computer simulations using parameters from a large 5 MVA permanent magnet synchronous generator installed at HPP “Bočac 2”, near the city of Banja Luka.

articleTitle: Iterative WPT Shielding Design and its Impact on Different WPT Key Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: Within the scope of this work, the key parameters self-inductance, mutual inductance and coupling factor of a wireless power transfer (WPT) 3D model are evaluated using finite element analysis (FEA). The height and width values of a passive shielding configuration are changed iteratively and the results are compared accordingly. Furthermore, the protection against the magnetic field is examined in compliance with the defined parameters of the ICNIRP (International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection) and the IEEE/ICES (International Committee on Electromagnetic Safety) for the different shielding constellations. The results of this study provide information about the ideal dimensions of a passive WPT shielding with maximum transmission efficiency.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Traditional Fractional Slot and Vernier RPMFS Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: In this paper the authors present the results of a comparative performance analysis for Rotor Permanent Magnet Flux Switching (RPMFS) machines having several different stator slot, stator pole and rotor pole combinations. The investigated combinations of stator slots and poles, as well as rotor poles are chosen taking into account the theory of air-gap magnetic field modulation or magnetic gearing. The presented machines include both traditional fractional slot machines, where the stator winding and the rotor PMs have the same number of poles, and non-traditional Vernier machines, where the stator winding and the rotor PMs have different pole numbers depending on the number of flux modulating stator slots. All analyzed machines are designed for the same rated torque, speed and voltage and have the same outer diameter, slot filling factor, and current density in conductors, in order to have a fair comparison of torque density between machines with different slot-pole combinations. The machines are designed and evaluated by a custom program based on 2D magnetostatic FEA developed by the authors. Although Vernier machines are generally claimed to have a superior torque density in recent publications, results presented in this paper show that the achievable torque density of Vernier RPMFS machines is similar to that of traditional fractional slot RPMFS machines.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of the Cascade Delay Cancellation in Enhanced Frequency-Locked Loops
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: Frequency-locked loops are essential elements for the power converters' synchronization as they are used for parameter estimation. However, the fundamental Frequency-Locked Loop structure shows sensitivity to the presence of DC offset and harmonics in the input signal. Those disturbances are causing oscillations in the estimated grid parameters making this technique unusable in those scenarios. The enhanced Frequency-Locked Loop called DC-FLL, solved DC offset sensitivity by introducing a new loop for its estimation and rejection. This paper presents a further modification of the DC-FLL, which is resistant to the presence of harmonics, by applying a Cascade Delay Signal Cancellation. This modification is able to maintain immunity to DC offset, the heritage of the DC-FLL, and also gain immunity to harmonics due to the Cascade Delay Signal Cancellation. To evaluate performance, the experimental setup was prepared and conducted. In the experiment, a few tests were verified by using an acquisition card and the MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Advanced Analysis of Arabidopsis thaliana Leaf Traits Using RGB Imaging and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: Image-based high-throughput plant phenotyping utilises various imaging techniques to automatically and non-invasively understand the growth of different plant species. These innovative imaging infrastructures are implemented to monitor plant development over time in indoor or outdoor environments. However, understanding the relationship between genotype and phenotype interactions under different environments remains challenging. This research study demonstrates superior extraction of leaf morphological features of different Arabidopsis thaliana ecotypes by analysing leaf geometry using a sequence of RGB images. Upon successful extraction of anatomical features, leaf length and area are converted into physical coordinates. Furthermore, considering these leaf features as 1D signals, the Fourier Spectrum is analysed, and most descriptive features are selected using PCA. Finally, leaf shape classification is established by training and testing five distinct ML models. A thorough evaluation of selected models demonstrates superiority in classifying two common leaf shapes of Arabidopsis plants.

articleTitle: Decentralised Planning of Production Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 XV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: This paper presents a distributed manufacturing operations management method in which the entities involved in manufacturing are divided into Product Agents and Resource Agents. The Product Agent represents the product to be manufactured, while the Resource Agent represents the manufacturing, transportation or storage unit. This way of implementing manufacturing operations is one of the key elements of the Industry 4.0 vision.
